item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft SharePoint: Enhanced data access governance reports and site access reviews
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft SharePoint is enhancing data access governance reports and site access reviews to give SharePoint admins more control, flexibility, and transparency when identifying and addressing potential data exposure. These updates help admins prioritize sites that may present the greatest data risk, direct review requests to the appropriate recipients, and track whether notifications were delivered.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): We will begin rolling out in late November 2026 and expect to complete by early December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • SharePoint admins who use data access governance reports and initiate site access reviews

Platforms and services

  • SharePoint Online
  • SharePoint admin center
  • Data access governance reports
  • Site access reviews

What will happen

  • The Site permissions across your organization report will show the number of files flagged by sensitive information types, such as credit card numbers, Social Security numbers, and custom-defined patterns.
  • SharePoint admins will be able to use this information to prioritize sites that may present greater data risk.
  • Admins will be able to direct site access review requests to site owners or site admins.
  • Admins will be able to send either one consolidated review email to all recipients or separate emails to individual recipients.

  • Admins will be able to view email delivery status and the complete recipient list for review requests.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required before rollout. We recommend that SharePoint admins:

  • Review current site permissions and data access governance processes.
  • Inform relevant SharePoint admins about the enhanced reporting and site access review capabilities.
  • Update internal documentation and workflows as appropriate.
  • Confirm that site owners and site admins are prepared to receive and complete site access review requests.

Learn more

  • Data access governance reports for SharePoint sites - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
  • Initiate site access reviews for Data access governance reports - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

ConsiderationExplanation
Does the change alter how existing customer data is accessed or processed?Yes. The Site permissions across your organization report will display counts of files flagged by sensitive information types. 
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. SharePoint admins will receive additional reporting information about files flagged by sensitive information types and greater visibility into site access review recipients and email delivery status.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. SharePoint admins will be able to select review recipients and choose between consolidated and individual review emails.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams Mobile: Introducing shared call history in the Queues app
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing shared call history in the Queues app on Microsoft Teams mobile, allowing authorized call queue representatives to view calls handled across their queue. This includes missed, answered, outgoing, and voicemail calls. By extending the existing desktop experience to mobile, we are helping teams coordinate customer follow-ups, avoid duplicate callbacks, and manage calls more efficiently while working away from their desks.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Representatives and supervisors with access to shared call history in the Queues app, which is included with a Teams Premium license.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams mobile, Queues app

What will happen

  • Authorized representatives can view shared call history across their call queue, including missed, answered, outgoing, and voicemail calls. Shared call history on mobile uses the same administrative settings as the desktop experience.

  • Users can filter call history by resolution status to identify calls that need attention.

  • Users can tap a call to view details, including the caller, call type, time, voicemail or forwarding information, and a timeline of the call's progression through the queue.

  • The system automatically marks missed calls as Unresolved, allowing representatives to identify customers who need follow-up.
  • Users can change missed call statuses to In progress or Resolved. All queue members with access to shared call history can see the updated status, who made the change, and when.
  • Users without shared call history enabled will continue to see only their personal call history.

[Action required and recommendations]

No new administrative action is required for this rollout. We recommend that you inform call queue representatives about the new mobile experience, particularly how to update missed call statuses to avoid duplicate follow-ups.

  • If your organization already uses shared call history, eligible users will automatically receive the mobile experience.
  • If shared call history is not enabled, you can enable it in the Teams admin center by creating a Shared Call History template and assigning it to your call queues. You can grant access to all queue members or restrict access to authorized users.

[Learn more]

  • Planning - Shared Call History for voice applications - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Audio announcement for Recording and Transcription
item.description:

The recording feature in Microsoft Teams now supports an audio announcement for Teams meetings and calls. With this new functionality, admins can enable a policy that plays an audio announcement when recording or transcription starts. This can be applied tenant-wide or to specific groups. The announcement helps ensure allowed participants who are permitted by policy are informed and improves accessibility awareness. This setting is available in both Meeting Policy and Calling Policy.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by early January 2027.

General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out on mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

General Availability (GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out on mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

None.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required. The default audio announcement policy is OFF; it can be turned on as needed.

[Compliance considerations:]

item.title: [planForChange] Changes to site logo URL metadata in SharePoint search results
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We are making a change to how SharePoint site logo URLs are maintained in search metadata to improve search indexing efficiency and reliability.

Going forward, changes to a SharePoint site's logo URL will no longer automatically update the SiteLogoUrl property on individual files and other items within that site.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 and expect to complete by early March 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

The SiteLogoUrl property will continue to be maintained for SharePoint sites. Individual items may retain a previously indexed SiteLogoUrl value, even after the site's logo changes. Applications or custom solutions that retrieve this property from individual items through search APIs may receive an outdated value.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

In the unlikely case that your organization uses the SiteLogoUrl property from individual search results, we recommend retrieving the current site logo directly from the associated SharePoint site instead. No action is required if your organization does not rely on this property.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: End of support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft Teams is ending support for upcoming builds on iOS 17 and iPadOS 17. As this change rolls out, new Teams releases will require iOS 18 or later on iPhone and iPadOS 18 or later on iPad.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by early January 2027.

Users whose devices remain on iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 will not be able to install newer Teams releases that require a newer operating system.

Teams versions already installed on these devices will continue functioning without official support. This change does not introduce a block on opening or signing in to those existing installations.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Identify devices running iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 and notify affected users.
  • Advise users to upgrade to a supported operating system, then update Teams through the Apple App Store, to continue receiving supported Teams releases.
  • Review any mobile device management (MDM) or app deployment policies that pin or require specific iOS/iPadOS versions, and update them to allow iOS 18/iPadOS 18 so affected devices are not blocked from upgrading.
  • Update internal support documentation and helpdesk guidance.

Learn more: Hardware requirements for Microsoft Teams.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 admin center: Unified release preferences for Standard, Deferred, and Frontier
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We're introducing a unified release preferences experience in the Microsoft 365 admin center. This brings together Standard release, Deferred release, and Frontier settings, making it easier to manage when users receive eligible generally available features and who participates in eligible preview experiences.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by end of November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected: Administrators managing release preferences for their organization.

Platforms/Services: Microsoft 365 admin center (Settings > Org settings > Release preferences); Microsoft 365 Copilot release preferences; Targeted Release.

What will happen:

  • Administrators will manage these settings in the unified Release preferences panel under Settings > Org settings > Release preferences.
  • Standard or Deferred release determines when users receive eligible generally available features. Standard users receive features as they roll out to the Standard audience. Deferred users receive eligible major features approximately 30 days after the start of their Standard rollout, allowing additional preparation time.
  • Frontier provides optional participation in eligible public preview experiences, independent of the Standard or Deferred preference. For example, users can participate in Frontier previews while remaining on Deferred release for eligible generally available features.
  • Organizations can set Standard or Deferred as their organization's release preference and assign selected users to the opposite preference through individual assignments or Microsoft Entra ID security groups.
  • Existing Standard/Deferred selections and exception assignments configured under Copilot release preferences: General availability will carry forward into the unified experience. The existing Copilot Frontier entry point will remain available and open the unified panel with Frontier settings in focus.
  • Existing Targeted Release settings will remain visible in the unified experience, but administrators will not be able to modify them or enroll new users or organizations in Targeted Release. Existing configurations will continue to apply to features delivered through that model until retirement. This update does not change the separately communicated Targeted Release retirement schedule.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • No action is required to receive the unified experience or to carry forward your existing Standard/Deferred configuration.
  • Review your organization's release preference, exception assignments, and Frontier participation.
  • Update internal administrator guidance to reflect the unified experience.
  • Organizations currently using Targeted Release should also review the separately communicated retirement guidance.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] Microsoft Entra ID: Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for SMS and voice multi-factor authentication
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Entra ID is adding safeguards to protect telephony-based multifactor authentication (MFA) from automated fraudulent activity. Some users who use SMS or voice for MFA may be asked to complete a risk-based anti-bot verification step (CAPTCHA) before Microsoft sends an SMS verification code or initiates a verification call.

This change is separate from the planned retirement of SMS and voice authentication and does not affect the retirement timeline.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Worldwide: Beginning in mid-November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who use SMS or voice for Microsoft Entra ID multifactor authentication

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • SMS and voice authentication methods

What will happen

  • Some users may be prompted to complete a risk-based anti-bot verification step (CAPTCHA) before Microsoft sends an SMS verification code or initiates a verification call.
  • The verification step will appear only for authentication attempts that meet sufficiently high-risk thresholds.
  • Users with restrictive network or firewall settings may be unable to complete SMS or voice MFA if the verification experience cannot load.

[Action required and recommendations]

We recommend that administrators take the following actions:

  • Prepare your help desk and notify users that some SMS and voice MFA attempts may require an additional CAPTCHA verification step.
  • Review the risk-based anti-bot verification documentation for network-readiness guidance. If your organization uses restrictive firewalls, proxies, or web filtering, ensure that the required resources can load during authentication.
  • Continue moving users to phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, where possible.

Learn more

  • Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for telephony-based sign-in - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Understanding telephony fraud risk for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Viva Insights: New Power BI report publishing capabilities for leaders
item.description:
Updated November 16, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We are expanding report publishing capabilities in Microsoft Viva Insights to include leaders, such as chief officers, managers, and their delegates. As part of this update, in Viva Feature Access Management, the Analyst report publish setting will be renamed to Report publish. This setting, which is on by default, will continue to be managed by Global Admins and Insights Admins, and will govern publishing for both analysts and leaders. This update enables leaders to directly publish and distribute curated Power BI reports available in Viva Insights without requiring an analyst to publish on their behalf.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide and GCC): Rollout begins in mid-December 2026 (previously early November) and is expected to complete by end of December 2026 (previously late November).

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Viva Insights report publishing capabilities.
  • Analysts, chief officers, managers, delegates, Insights Admins, and Global Admins.
  • Users who receive published Viva Insights reports.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Viva Insights
  • Power BI reports available through the Viva Insights Reports tab

What will happen

  • All analysts and leaders will be able to publish Power BI reports that are available to them in the Reports tab.
  • Users can publish either default or customized reports available to them.
  • Publishers can define the audience, report title, description, and publication end date.
  • Recipients will receive an email notification when a report is published to them, and can access published reports from the Viva Insights Reports tab.
  • Published reports can be shared using either: 
    • Unfiltered publish, where recipients view the report using the full data scope available for that report.
    • Manager-hierarchy publish, where recipients view the report based on the applicable manager hierarchy.
  • If a published report is configured to refresh weekly or monthly, the underlying query will continue to refresh until the publication end date.
  • Analysts and leaders will be able to manage published reports through the Manage publishes option.
  • Recipients can view and interact with published reports but cannot download reports, access row-level data, modify or manage publications, extend access, or republish reports.
  • If a publisher loses the qualifying role used to publish the report, recipients will retain access until the publication expires.
  • The existing Analyst report publish feature access control will be renamed to Report publish. This control will govern report publishing for analysts and leader personas, remains managed by Global Admins and Insights Admins, and is on by default.
  • Insights Admins will have visibility into published reports through the Admin Publish Reports experience, including the ability to view and remove publications and publish reports on behalf of users.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you review your organization's report publishing governance and processes prior to rollout.

[Learn more]

[Compliance considerations]

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Copilot Pages and Notebooks Creation in OneDrive
item.description:
Updated November 16, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We're changing where newly created Copilot Pages are stored. Going forward, Copilot Pages created in Copilot Chat, the Microsoft 365 Copilot app, and new Copilot Notebooks will be stored in OneDrive for Business instead of their current location.

This change enables organizations to manage newly created Copilot Pages using existing OneDrive for Business governance, compliance, data protection, retention, and lifecycle management capabilities.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-October 2026 (previously mid-August) and expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously late November)
  • General Availability (GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Beginning in mid-November 2026 (previously mid-September) and expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously early December)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

Users who create Copilot Pages in:

  • Copilot Chat
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot app
  • Copilot Notebooks

Microsoft 365 administrators responsible for governance, compliance, retention, and content management

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Copilot Chat
  • Copilot Notebooks
  • OneDrive for Business
  • Microsoft Purview compliance solutions

What will happen

After rollout:

  • Newly created Copilot Pages will be stored in users' OneDrive for Business.
  • New Copilot Pages will appear alongside other OneDrive files, such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint documents.
  • New Copilot Notebooks and artifacts created within them will appear alongside other OneDrive files, such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint documents.
  • Existing OneDrive governance, compliance, data protection, retention, lifecycle management, reporting, and investigation capabilities will apply to newly created Copilot Pages.

In addition to all existing governance and management capabilities, the following additional OneDrive for Business capabilities will apply to newly created Copilot Pages:

Compliance and legal

  • Standard file path-based eDiscovery
  • Retention labels with record locking
  • Information Barriers
  • Compliance Boundaries

Data protection

  • Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies and mitigation workflows
  • Third-party governance solutions that support OneDrive content

Lifecycle management

  • Retention and lifecycle policies
  • Existing departed-user workflows for OneDrive content

Monitoring and oversight

  • OneDrive storage reporting
  • Administrative investigations of content stored in OneDrive

Unaffected files

  • Existing Copilot Pages will remain in their current location and will not be migrated as part of this change.
  • Existing Copilot Notebooks will continue to store all newly created pages in SharePoint Embedded. Only Copilot Notebooks created after this change will store pages in OneDrive. 
  • Loop workspaces are not affected and will continue to use their current storage location.

IT Admin controls

  • If your organization has set Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks to Disabled, that setting will continue to be honored after this change.
  • This admin control is planned for future retirement. Microsoft will provide additional communication and transition guidance before the setting is retired.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required for the rollout.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review existing DLP, retention, and compliance policies that apply to OneDrive for Business.
  • Verify that any third-party governance or eDiscovery solutions are configured to monitor OneDrive content as appropriate.
  • Update internal documentation and governance guidance for AI-generated content.
  • Communicate to users that newly created Copilot Pages will be stored in their OneDrive for Business.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change alter where customer data is stored?Yes. Newly created Copilot Pages will be stored in OneDrive for Business instead of their previous storage location.
Does this change affect compliance and governance capabilities?Yes. Newly created Copilot Pages will be subject to OneDrive for Business compliance capabilities, including eDiscovery, retention labels with record locking, Information Barriers, and Compliance Boundaries.
Does this change affect data protection controls?Yes. Existing OneDrive for Business data protection controls, including Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies and supported third-party governance solutions, can be applied to newly created Copilot Pages.
Does this change affect lifecycle management and retention processes?Yes. Existing OneDrive for Business retention policies, lifecycle management capabilities, and departed-user workflows will apply to newly created Copilot Pages.
Does this change affect how administrators monitor or investigate content?Yes. Administrators will be able to use standard OneDrive for Business reporting, monitoring, and investigation capabilities for newly created Copilot Pages.

item.title: [planForChange] Dynamics 365 and Power Platform– Information about storage validation for Dataverse-only tenants
item.description:
We plan to introduce staged storage validation for supported Dynamics 365 applications no earlier than January 2027, with finalized rollout timing expected to be shared by early December 2026. This change will give administrators clearer visibility into storage usage and advance notice of potential restrictions. To prepare, administrators should review storage usage and address capacity gaps by removing unnecessary data, purchasing additional capacity, or enabling pay-as-you-go for sandbox environments.

If no corrective action is initiated after repeated notifications, when a tenant exceeds its entitled Database, File, or Log capacity, environment creation, copy, restore, convert trial to paid, recover operations, and add Dataverse to an environment operations will be restricted immediately. If the overage remains unresolved, sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go billing enabled will enter Administration mode after 30 days of remaining over capacity, allowing access only to administrators. After 90 days from the date the tenant exceeds capacity, affected sandbox environments will be disabled and will no longer be accessible to users. During this phase customers can contact Microsoft Support for the sole purpose of directing data export options, if needed.

Production environments are not subject to administration mode and disabled stage restrictions and will remain accessible. However, environment creation, copy, restore, convert trial to paid, recover operations and add Dataverse to an environment operations will remain blocked while the tenant is over capacity.

How does this affect me?
The Dataverse storage validation applies only to Dataverse-only tenants without Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations environment(s) or consumption. The following products are included in the storage validation rollout:
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Voice
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact Center
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Project Operations (Dataverse deployments)
If your tenant exceeds its entitled storage capacity, the following lifecycle applies:

Stage Timing Impact
1. Restricted When the tenant first exceeds its entitled storage capacity, known as time zero (T0) Environment creation, copy, restore, convert trial to paid, recover operations, and add Dataverse to an environment are blocked immediately when the tenant exceeds its entitled capacity.
2. Administration mode After 30 unresolved days from T0 Only administrators can sign in to *affected sandbox environments. All other users are blocked from accessing the environment.
3. Disabled After 90 unresolved days from T0 All users, including administrators, are blocked from accessing *affected sandbox environments; the environment data is retained and remains available for recovery before and after remediation. During this phase, if the tenant remains in overage, customers can contact Microsoft Support for the sole purpose of directing data export options, if needed. All other mechanisms designed to resolve overage are also available to customers at this phase.

Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing do not progress through the storage overage lifecycle even if the tenant remains over storage capacity. Other *affected sandbox environments in the tenant may still be affected with restrictions.

We will provide notifications that include the tenant's current storage status, the date it first exceeded capacity, its current lifecycle stage, future restrictions, and recommended remediation actions.

Admins can exit Administration Mode at any time; however, the overage lifecycle continues as long as the tenant remains over its entitled storage capacity. Once the tenant returns below 100%, no further restrictions are applied. Environments do not automatically return to their previous state; admins must manually exit Administration Mode or re-enable them, as applicable. Processing time may vary depending on the remediation method used.

What action do I need to take?
Review your environment(s) and perform the following actions before January 2027:
  • Review Database, File, and Log capacity in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Remove or archive data that is no longer needed.
  • Establish data governance policies in your environment to help prevent future storage overages.
  • Purchase additional capacity or configure pay-as-you-go.
  • Invite makers and users to become aware of these potential restrictions and to notify administrators about possible areas of adjustment.
  • Review your release activities that depend on sandbox availability, and plan accordingly.
For additional information, please visit the following articles:

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Field Service - Preserve actual booking End Time when completion is recorded later
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to Preserve actual booking End Time when completion is recorded later in Dynamics 365 Field Service. This feature will reach public preview on November 22, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature allows Field Service administrators to choose whether completion by the booked resource automatically changes the booking End Time. Admins complete bookings later can preserve the existing or explicitly supplied work end, helping booking duration and downstream time and cost records remain aligned with when the work occurred.

Use the organization-level Set End Time on booked resource completion setting in Field Service settings to control the automatic End Time update.
  • With the setting set to Yes, which is the default, current behavior is preserved. When the booked resource completes a booking without supplying End Time, Field Service sets End Time to the completion time and recalculates Duration.
  • With the setting set to No, Field Service preserves End Time and Duration when the booked resource completes the booking unless the completion request explicitly supplies a different End Time.
  • Completion by another user or an integration continues to preserve End Time for either setting value.
  • When the setting is No and the booked resource completes the booking, Field Service uses the retained or supplied End Time as the effective Completed booking timestamp. This keeps timestamp-derived booking journals and automatic time entries aligned with the recorded work end. Dataverse audit fields continue to show when the completion was submitted.
The setting applies to future completion transitions and does not rewrite historical bookings. It does not change the booking-status lifecycle, invoice generation, or the existing Work Order Completed On calculation, which continues to use the latest eligible booking End Time.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

item.title: [planForChange] Release Planner Retirement: D365, Power Platform, and Dataverse Move to AI at Work

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Purview: Adaptive scopes add lifecycle status evaluation controls for recipients and site owners
item.description:

[What and why]

Microsoft Purview is introducing lifecycle status evaluation controls for adaptive scopes. This update gives administrators explicit control over whether active, inactive, and soft-deleted recipients and site owners are included in adaptive scope membership.

With this change, newly created adaptive scopes will evaluate only active recipients and site owners by default. Administrators can configure adaptive scopes to include inactive and/or soft-deleted recipients and site owners when needed.

This update also adds support for ISO 8601 duration values for selected date attributes in the adaptive scope advanced query builder.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 568785.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview: Beginning in December 2026 (previously mid-September) and expected to complete in December 2026 (previously early October)

  • Organizations that use adaptive scopes for Microsoft Purview policy targeting.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview
  • Adaptive Scopes

What will happen

Existing adaptive scopes will continue to function as they do today and will not be automatically modified as part of this rollout.

For newly created adaptive scopes:

  • Active recipients and site owners will be evaluated by default.
  • Inactive and soft-deleted recipients or site owners will not be included unless explicitly configured by an administrator.

Administrators will also have the option to update existing adaptive scopes to use explicit lifecycle status evaluation criteria for recipients and site owners.

Additionally, adaptive scopes will support ISO 8601 duration values for certain date-based attributes in the advanced query builder.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Manage call groups on Mobile

When availability changes, for example when a backup contact is out or a new teammate needs to cover, users often notice while they are away from their desks and cannot update their call group from the phone where they take their calls.

We're introducing the ability to create and manage a call group directly from Microsoft Teams on Mobile. Users can add or remove members, configure how the group should ring, and choose to forward or simultaneously ring incoming calls to their call group. This makes it easier for on the go users to manage how their calls are handled without needing to reach desktop.

From Settings, users can open Calling and select Manage call group to view their current call group or create a new one.

Once the call group is set up, users can forward their calls to the group or ring the group at the same time as their own devices, using the call handling options in Calling settings.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on early December 2026 and expect to complete by mid December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users will be able to:

  • View their current call group and its members.
  • Create a call group if they don't have one.
  • Add or remove members.
  • Choose how the group rings: Everyone at once or In the order below.
  • Reorder members when the ring order matters.
  • Forward calls to the call group or have the group ring alongside their own devices.

Changes made on Mobile apply to the same call group settings that users manage on desktop. Mobile adds a new way to manage them and does not introduce a separate call group.

This feature is available to users with a Teams Phone license and uses the existing calling policy that controls call groups. If call groups are turned off for a user in their calling policy, they won't be able to use the feature on Mobile.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Update internal documentation to clarify that saving a generated table of contents requires edit permissions on the PDF.
  • Encourage users to validate AI-generated table-of-contents entries when accuracy is important.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed? Yes. Copilot processes PDF content that the licensed user is already authorized to access in order to generate a table of contents for navigation. Existing file permissions are respected, and saving changes requires edit permissions.
  • Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data? Yes. Copilot analyzes PDF document structure and generates an AI-created hierarchical table of contents. The experience is user-initiated and does not run automatically.
  • Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI? Yes. Eligible users can request Copilot to generate a table of contents for PDF files that do not already contain one.
  • Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves? Yes. The feature is user-initiated and only runs when a licensed user chooses to generate a Smart TOC.

The experience will clearly indicate that the table of contents was AI generated and may contain inaccuracies.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Facilitator proactively detects and resolves knowledge gaps in meetings
item.description:
Updated November 12, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why]

We are introducing a new Microsoft Teams Facilitator capability that proactively detects and resolves knowledge gaps during meetings. Facilitator can identify when participants ask questions or express uncertainty and retrieve and share relevant answers using web search in the meeting chat. This enhancement helps improve meeting productivity by reducing interruptions and enabling teams to stay focused on goals while accessing needed information. If a participant asks a factual question and no one responds, Facilitator can provide an answer directly in the meeting chat.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 558341.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning early February 2027 (previously early December) and expected to complete mid-February 2027 (previously mid-December)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning mid-February 2027 (previously mid-December) and expected to complete early March 2027 (previously mid-January)

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

  • Users in Microsoft Teams meetings where Facilitator is enabled with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Teams (meetings)
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Facilitator will monitor meeting conversations in real time to detect implicit or explicit information needs.
  • When a knowledge gap is identified, Facilitator performs a web search and posts a response in the meeting chat: 
  • Responses are infrequent in practice and typically occur less than once per meeting.
  • Responses are limited to questions relevant to the meeting discussion based on agenda signals and conversational context.
  • Facilitator must be manually added to the meeting and is not enabled by default.
  • A user with a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license must enable Facilitator for the meeting. Other participants do not need to be licensed to receive responses.
  • Admins can disable Facilitator at the tenant level. The feature depends on the Copilot web search setting. If web search is disabled, responses are not generated.
  • Users can stop the behavior at any time by removing Facilitator from the meeting.
  • The feature is supported in standard Teams meetings only and not supported in calls, webinars, or town halls.
  • The experience is supported in meetings that include external or cross-tenant participants.

[Action Required/Recommendations]

No immediate action is required.

Recommended actions:

  • Review your organization’s Copilot web search and Facilitator configuration settings to confirm alignment with your policies.
  • Inform helpdesk and users about proactive Facilitator responses in meeting chats.
  • Update internal documentation or training materials if you reference Teams meeting experiences.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (for example, meeting conversations)?Yes. The feature processes meeting conversations in real time to detect knowledge gaps and generate responses.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI or machine learning capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. Facilitator uses AI to interpret meeting content and generate contextual responses during meetings.
Does the change provide end users with a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users receive proactive, AI-generated responses within the Teams meeting chat without needing to prompt the system.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through configuration settings?Yes. The feature depends on the Copilot web search setting, which admins can enable or disable to control functionality.
Does the change allow a user to enable or disable the feature themselves?Yes. Users can stop the behavior by removing Facilitator from the meeting.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Windows: Updates to address compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys
item.description:
Updated November 11, 2026: On November 16, 2026, an update will be released for Microsoft Edge and WebView2, delivered via the PKI Metadata component, which will fully remove default trust for the remaining roots (emSign Root CA - G1, emSign Root CA - C1, emSign ECC Root CA, and emSign Root TLS CA - G1). Devices check for PKI Metadata updates every 10 hours and shortly after each new app launch. 

For more information, see Microsoft Response to eMudhra Certificate Authority Key Compromise.

[What and why]

Microsoft is responding to an issue involving eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority (CA) private keys, six associated with TLS and two with code signing. Because these keys could be recovered, they could potentially be used to create certificates or sign content that appeared to come from a trusted CA. The issue arose in eMudhra's certificate hierarchy and was not a compromise of Microsoft systems.

Microsoft is updating certificate trust to block affected certificate authorities and remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Windows, Microsoft Edge, or WebView2, particularly organizations with certificates that chain to one of the eight certificates being removed
  • Organizations managing disconnected Windows devices or disconnected Azure devices may need to take additional action

Platforms and services

  • Windows
  • Microsoft Edge
  • WebView2
  • Azure virtual machines

What will happen

  • Microsoft has published an update to the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List to block the affected certificate authorities.
  • Microsoft has deployed a separate CRLSet update for Microsoft Edge and WebView2 to block affected TLS certificates signed by the affected certificate authorities.
  • The Microsoft Edge and WebView2 update is delivered automatically through the component update mechanism. Customers do not need to install a new browser version.
  • Microsoft has released updates to Windows and Microsoft Edge to remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies from their trust lists.
  • After these updates reach a device, the affected certificates will no longer be trusted by default through the respective trust lists.

[Action required and recommendations]

  • Keep updates flowing. Allow automatic Windows certificate trust updates and Microsoft Edge component updates to reach your devices.
  • Check disconnected Windows devices. If you manage Windows devices that do not receive automatic updates, make sure your update process delivers the updated Disallowed Certificate Trust List and upcoming trust-list changes. See the Microsoft Learn guidance in Learn more for information about distributing certificate trust lists in disconnected environments.
  • Review disconnected Azure devices. Review disconnected Azure devices running on Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) or single-instance VMs. Updated images are available in Azure Marketplace, and customers can deploy them to protect against this vulnerability.
  • Replace dependent certificates. If any of your certificates chain to one of the seven certificates being removed, identify those dependencies and obtain replacement certificates or an alternative trusted chain before the changes reach your devices.

Learn more

  • Microsoft’s response to compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys
  • Configure trusted roots and disallowed certificates in Windows | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Copilot Studio - Set up third-party agent connections in conversations
item.description:
We are announcing improvements to the experience of setting up connections in chats with Copilot Studio agents. These improvements will reach general availability by December 31, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Previously, users needed to leave their conversation, go to a separate connection-management experience, complete setup, and then restart their interaction. This feature is introducing a more seamless way for users to connect agents to third-party services. When an agent requires a connection, users will be guided through a focused setup experience without leaving the conversation or being redirected to the full connection-management portal. When possible, the agent will reuse an existing valid connection.

With this update:
  • Users can establish a required third-party connection from their agent conversation.
  • Users complete only the setup required for the service they are using.
  • Users return directly to the conversation after connecting.
  • An eligible existing connection can be reused instead of configuring another connection.
  • Users can continue working with connected agents across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams, and Web Chat.
  • Existing organizational controls that govern which connectors and connections users can access will continue to determine availability.
Please note that developers of agents published through a custom web UI using the Standard harness will be required to make changes to support the new connection experience.

What action do I need to take?
To prepare for this change, we recommend that you:
  • Inform support teams and agent users about the improved connection experience.
  • Review your existing organizational controls for connectors and connections.
For agents published through a custom web UI using the Standard harness, update your implementation to:
  • Open the new connection window.
  • Continue the conversation after connection setup succeeds.
If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Support connection setup in a custom canvas.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: Filter responses by content source
item.description:
[What and why]

We're introducing content source filters in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. This feature allows users to scope a prompt to specific content sources so that Copilot grounds its response only in the sources they select. This helps users focus responses on the most relevant Microsoft 365 content, as well as connected or available third-party sources, while maintaining existing permission and access controls.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users licensed for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat

What will happen

  • Users will see a source selection control in the Copilot Chat prompt area.
  • Users can select one or more available content sources to limit retrieval and grounding for a specific prompt to those sources.
  • Available sources reflect the content sources enabled in your tenant, including Graph connectors and federated connectors available to users.
  • This feature changes where Copilot retrieves information for a prompt and does not change what content a user is permitted to access. Data access, compliance boundaries, and tenant data handling remain unchanged.
  • If no source is selected, Copilot Chat behavior remains unchanged and will use its default orchestration across available sources.
  • Responses will continue to include citations that reflect the selected sources.
  • Source selection applies only to the current prompt and does not persist across sessions.
  • This feature is enabled by default for users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Copilot source selection

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Review the display names of published Graph connectors, ensuring that they are clear and recognizable, as these names will appear in the source selection experience for users.
  • Verify the health and search permissions of connectors that should be available to users. Connectors in an error or unpublished state will not appear.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Outlook: Update to default blocked file types in OwaMailboxPolicy
item.description:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

To enhance security in Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, we are updating the default list of blocked file types in OwaMailboxPolicy. As part of this update, the .msix and .msixbundle file types will be added to the BlockedFileTypes list in the default OWA Mailbox policy and any custom policies created in your tenant. Most organizations are not expected to be affected by this update because these file types are infrequently used. This update is part of our ongoing efforts to strengthen security and help protect organizations from potentially unsafe file attachments.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout begins in early December 2026 (previously early November) and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously mid-November).

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Exchange Online administrators who manage OWA mailbox policies
  • Users who send or receive .msix or .msixbundle attachments in Outlook on the web or new Outlook for Windows

Platforms and services

  • Outlook for the web
  • New Outlook for Windows
  • Exchange Online

What will happen

  • The .msix and .msixbundle file types will be added to the BlockedFileTypes list in all OWA Mailbox policies in your organization, including the default policy and any custom policies created in your tenant.
  • Users who send or receive .msix or .msixbundle attachments in Outlook on the web or new Outlook for Windows will no longer be able to open or download them.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required if your organization does not rely on the .msix or .msixbundle file types. If your organization relies on these file types, we recommend that you add them to the AllowedFileTypes property of your users' OwaMailboxPolicy objects prior to rollout.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Malicious QR code detection in messages
item.description:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Teams is extending malicious URL protection to provide near-real-time detection of malicious destinations embedded in QR codes shared in messages. Teams will analyze QR code destinations to identify potential phishing and fraud threats and display an additional warning when malicious content is detected.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously mid-November)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who use Microsoft Teams messaging

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams chats, meeting chats, and channels

What will happen

  • Teams will decode and evaluate QR code destinations in inline images shared in 1:1 chats, group chats, meeting chats, and channels.
  • Detection applies to internal and external communications.
  • Images containing QR codes from external senders are already blurred by default. When Teams identifies a malicious QR code, users will also see the warning, “This message contains a link that might be harmful,” and a “Learn about file and link safety” link.
  • QR code images from internal senders are not blurred by default. The same warning will appear when Teams detects a malicious QR code.
  • For users on Teams mobile in China, QR code images are blurred by default regardless of whether the sender is internal or external, and any messages containing malicious QR code will be blocked.
  • Malicious QR code detection is managed by the existing Malicious URL protection setting.
  • The setting is enabled by default. Organizations with Malicious URL protection enabled will automatically receive malicious QR code detection as the feature rolls out.
  • No separate configuration is available or required for malicious QR code detection.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required.

Admins can review or change the existing Malicious URL protection setting in Teams admin center > Settings and policies > Messaging Safety.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform users and help desk staff about the additional warning for detected malicious QR codes.
  • Clarify that QR code blurring is a separate precautionary experience and does not mean that Teams has identified a QR code as malicious.
  • Review internal documentation about Teams messaging security and update it if necessary.
